fullarm:
Context from a materials paper:
- Percutaneous implants need a tight skin seal; bare Ti lets epithelium grow down along the implant and a fibrous capsule form
- Ti implant surface carrying a hydroxyapatite nanorod coating as the base
- Hydrothermal growth of HA and Si-HA nanorod coatings on Ti
- Si is incorporated in the Si-HA nanorods at about 3-5% and is absent from HA
- Si sits on phosphate sites as orthosilicate SiO4 4- replacing PO4 3- in the HA lattice
- Si substitution distorts the HA lattice: reflections shift to lower angle and the a-axis lengthens slightly (9.425 to 9.437 A)
- Si-HA releases more Ca than HA at every immersion time and also releases Si (~0.5-0.6 ppm by 28 d)
- Ions released from Si-HA (Si and extra Ca) stimulate fibroblast TGF-b1/CTGF signalling, driving alpha-SMA, Col-I and collagen production
- Si-HA up-regulates fibrogenic genes (TGF-b1, CTGF, alpha-SMA, Col-I) in fibroblasts above HA and Ti

Panels:
- F8b: caption: Fig. 8. Gene expressions of fibroblasts cultured on different surfaces after incubation for 3, and 7 days ... CTGF | condition: CTGF
- F8c: caption: Fig. 8. Gene expressions of fibroblasts cultured on different surfaces after incubation for 3, and 7 days ... -SMA | condition: -SMA
- F8d: caption: Fig. 8. Gene expressions of fibroblasts cultured on different surfaces after incubation for 3, and 7 days ... Col-I | condition: Col-I

Question: The text claims Si-HA drives higher fibrogenic gene expression in fibroblasts (CTGF, alpha-SMA, Col-I) than HA and Ti, with the same ranking holding at every time point. Do the mRNA panels in Figure 8b-8d support this?

key.answer_key: No. At 3 d the alpha-SMA panel (F8c) shows essentially no difference across conditions (~1.0, 1.13, 1.11), and the CTGF (F8b) and Col-I (F8d) panels show HA and Si-HA at about the same level, contradicting the text's claim of the same ranking order at each time point (o22).
